title: The Great Muffin Delivery
markdown:
Some days feel grey even if you have seen the aurora dance and the Sahara lie like a sea of gold. Suri’s grey came from a sniffle that was not hers. Leo, her very best pal, was tucked in bed with a tickly cough. She had baked berry muffins bursting with flavour. They sat on the cooling rack, useless as treasure locked in a tower. How did yum become help inside a boy?

“It’s no use, Pebble,” she told the muffins. “They’re too good to sit here. But how do they get there? Inside Leo, I mean.” She had considered a straw all the way to his tummy, and even her engineering goggles, perched like curious antennae, had voted against it.

Pebble the tortoise blinked. His shell was a miniature world of mossy bumps and hidden wisdom. He was not one for quick dashes. His adventures unfolded at the pace of a slow deliberate stroll, each step a thoughtful decision. He had once spent a whole afternoon contemplating a particularly fascinating dewdrop and considered it time well used.

“A delivery, you say? That sounds like a grand adventure.” His voice was pebbles shifting in a gentle stream. “A game about getting important things where they need to go. A tiny expedition, right inside Leo’s own body.”

Suri loved games. Her mind liked gears. She pulled her goggles down as if the floor might need measuring.

“The Red Ribbon Relay,” Pebble announced, fetching a long raspberry-bright ribbon from the craft box. “This is like the blood. The busiest highway. Always on the move.” From his shell, because tortoises keep surprising cupboards, he produced tiny paper circles. Blue ones: oxygen, the breath of life. Red-gold ones, marmalade-bright: the goodness from muffins. Nutrients. Fuel.

They spread the ribbon in a winding path that snaked like a playful worm. Leo’s body was the map. Pebble took one end, surprisingly spry.

“Imagine the heart.” A gentle squeeze, leathery neck stretching. “It pumps. Like a little engine that never clocks off.” He nudged the ribbon toward a pretend lung. A blue circle stuck as if it had been waiting. He jogged a little. The ribbon undulated. Suri held the other end, goggles bouncing.

“So the ribbon goes everywhere? Tippy-toe? Funny earlobe?”

“Everywhere.” Pebble’s voice was a steady rumble. “Toes, fingertips, brain. Every busy cell that keeps Leo laughing and playing his games. Every part wants a delivery.” He looped the ribbon around chair-legs that were, for this afternoon, organs. “Blood picks up oxygen from the lungs, and nutrients from the tummy once the muffins have been broken into tiny pieces. Then it carries them, a postman who never loses the addresses.”

Suri watched the ribbon flow, a vibrant stream weaving a tapestry across the playroom, a tiny tireless river from imaginary pinky to imaginary curly hair. If a part of Leo felt tired or weak, oxygen rode in. If a cough needed fighting, muffin-goodness rode in too, fuel for healing, packaged and sent. Not a straw to the tummy. A highway.

Her eyes widened. The sweet warm scent of the muffins seemed to surge with the idea. “So the muffins get broken down, and the good bits hop on the red ribbon like little delivery trucks with their engines running. Oxygen hops on too, to help Leo’s cells work and make him strong. A tiny factory, and the muffins are the raw materials!”

Pebble’s slow smile crinkled his eyes. “And the ribbon picks up waste, the bits cells are finished with, and takes those away. A complete service. Even when Leo is asleep.”

Suri bounced, engineering instincts buzzing. She grabbed a large piece of paper and her box of colourful crayons. Quick confident strokes: a big circle for Leo’s chest where the heart would be, a smaller for his head, then a winding intricate network of tubes. “The circulatory system!” She tapped the paper. “The body’s superhighway, mapped. The heart is the pump, that big red circle, and the blood is the fleet of delivery trucks, zipping around with oxygen and all the good stuff from my muffins. It takes the goodness everywhere so Leo’s cells can get strong and fight that sniffle.”

She placed a few drawn muffins near the tummy. “They go in here. Then the goodness gets on the red ribbon highway, and off it goes.” She imagined tiny particles of muffin zipping through Leo, warming him from the inside, giving him energy to chase a ball again, to laugh, to be his usual bouncy self. A hopeful smile chased the grey.

Pebble did not wonder aloud what other secrets bodies held. He coiled the ribbon into a neat loop, which is tortoise for job done, and eyed a muffin as if it too might need delivering, though only as far as a plate. Suri wrapped two for Leo, still warm, and drew a tiny red road on the napkin so the journey would not be lonely. Uncle Dev would take them round later; for now the highway on the floor still ran from lung to toe, and the blue circles clung, and the heart-end of the ribbon waited for the next squeeze.
characters: Suri (young engineer), Pebble (tortoise), Uncle Dev (uncle), Leo (friend)
author: StoryGen Community
